fields.subject: Model Mapping
fields.trigger: a mapping attribute's declared database type cannot accept the CLR type of the property or variable it maps, and the mapping layer raises InvalidMapTypeException
fields.response: raise it with the property (or, for a nested-model or shard-key variable that is not itself a model property, the variable's name and type), the provider's numeric database-type value, and — from the shared Mapper, the SQL Server TVP mapper and the Orleans grain mappers — the attribute's database type name, so the message reads "Sql type mismatch: Class {class} cannot map property “{property}” of type “{type}” to database type {name} ({number})." (or, for a variable, "Sql type mismatch: {variable} cannot be mapped because type {type} does not map to database type {name} ({number}).")
fields.postcondition: the PostgreSQL COPY mapper is the exception: it raises the property-and-number form without the type name, so its message reports only "database type enumeration with numeric value of {number}" and the caller must translate the NpgsqlDbType number itself. In the property forms the property name and the property type are each enclosed in a matched pair of curly quotes. In every form the exception's VariableName, VariableType and SqlType properties carry the same values as the message
